name: Zebulon Featherly
bio: Zebulon Featherly is an independent candidate for Michigan's 1st Congressional District in 2026. He grew up near Houghton on a small family farm, trained in wind energy at a trade school in Vancouver, Washington, and worked for about five years as a wind turbine technician; he is now based in Traverse City. He took part in a March 2026 candidate forum in Marquette.

platform.point: Runs without a party label, pledging to represent constituents rather than party interests.
Would push to raise the minimum wage, oppose new taxes on working families and have the very wealthy pay more.
Supports making universal health care and tuition-free higher education a reality.
Backs a clear, fair path to citizenship for people building their lives in the United States.
Calls gun ownership a fundamental right and says he would not take guns away but would seek responsible safeguards.
Proposes pay-as-you-go budgeting, lifting the Social Security payroll tax cap, drug-price negotiation and closer scrutiny of defense spending.
Opposes moving the U.S. Forest Service headquarters out of Washington and closing most of its research facilities.
Announced he would join the May 1, 2026 general strike, citing wealth inequality and corporate conduct toward workers.

economy.evidence: Pledges to raise the minimum wage, have extreme wealth pay more, lift the Social Security payroll tax cap and negotiate drug prices, and says billionaires should not exist.

welfare.evidence: Says he is committed to making universal health care and tuition-free higher education a reality.

liberty.evidence: Only guns are addressed: he calls gun ownership fundamental and says he would not take guns away but would push for responsible safeguards; abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights and speech are not addressed.

immigration.evidence: Supports a clear, fair path to citizenship for everyone building a life in America and welcoming immigrants who contribute.

energy.evidence: General statement: pledges to push clean energy advancements and environmental protection, while also citing domestic energy independence.

tech.evidence: General statement: pledges to stand against companies that profit from deception and criticizes tech billionaires profiting from users' attention.

education.evidence: Supports tuition-free public higher education; he has not addressed K-12 school choice or vouchers.

notes: Searched his campaign site pages (Where I Stand, My Story, Statements, Transparency) and forum coverage; his site says he worked as a wind turbine technician, while the factory-worker role comes from Wikipedia's candidate list and was not independently confirmed. No positions were found on abortion, drugs, policing and surveillance, foreign policy or religion.

name: Andy Maidment
current_role: Retired Army officer and IT security professional
bio: Andy Maidment is a retired officer who served 21 years in the U.S. Army and Missouri National Guard and now works in information technology security. He holds a history degree from Missouri State University and has lived in Missouri since age twelve. He is the Libertarian nominee for Missouri's 6th Congressional District in 2026.

platform.point: Calls taxation theft and argues the country prospered before the income tax, seeking to make the IRS unimportant.
Would eliminate the Departments of Education, Commerce and Homeland Security, which he says lack a constitutional basis.
Would require Congress to approve federal regulations before they take effect.
Wants to end surveillance powers created under the Patriot Act.
Supports expanding the right to keep and bear arms and protecting free speech.
Would bring U.S. troops home from the Middle East, keep a strong national defense and trade peacefully with other nations.
Criticizes COVID relief fraud and costly military technology programs, and aims to reduce the national debt.

economy.evidence: Calls taxation theft and wants Congress to approve regulations before they take effect.

welfare.evidence: General statement: argues taxes take money from those who produce and give it to those who do not; no specific program proposals.

liberty.evidence: Supports expanding gun rights and protecting free speech; abortion, drugs and LGBTQ rights are not addressed.

security.evidence: Wants to end Patriot Act surveillance and eliminate the Department of Homeland Security.

foreign.evidence: Calls for bringing troops home from the Middle East and ending what he calls the Forever War, favoring peaceful trade.

education.evidence: Would eliminate the federal Department of Education; he does not address vouchers or school choice directly.

notes: Found his campaign site through Wikipedia and read its Issues, About, Media and What is a Libertarian pages. No positions were found on immigration, energy, technology or religion.

name: Erik Kiehle
bio: Erik Kiehle is a property management businessman from the Meridian area of Lauderdale County, Mississippi, and the Libertarian nominee for Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District. He is a volunteer firefighter with two Lauderdale County departments and a private pilot.

platform.point: Describes himself as 'America First' and emphasizes national strength and security.
Says the nation should reflect equal opportunity, accountability and justice.
Pledges transparency and accountability to all constituents.
Promises to listen to local concerns and advocate for Mississippians.

notes: Re-read his one-page campaign site (its About, Values and Info sections are anchors on the home page) and Wikipedia's race page; only general themes are stated, so no positions were scored. His Facebook page could not be read without logging in.
